newsitem.title: NEPAL: Two South Koreans scale Mount Everest.
newsitem.headline: Two South Koreans scale Mount Everest.

text.p: Two South Koreans and three Nepali climbers successfully scaled the 8,848 metre (29,028 foot) summit of Mount Everest, the world's tallest peak, the Nepali tourism ministry said on Saturday.
Choi Jong-Tai, a 26 year-old electronics student, and Shin Kwang-Chal, a 25 year-old student of environmental studies, both from Kwangju city, scaled the peak from Nepal side on October 11.
The three Nepalis, who sucessfully reached the peak, were Panaru Sherpa, Dawa Tamang and Tipa Sherpa, officials said.
